conviction_note: The full-year upgrade is already out: the 18 Aug 2026 RNS said FY27 revenue and adjusted PBT would be 'comfortably ahead', the stock rose 22%, and Berenberg reset FY27 to about £540m revenue and £84m PBT. So the H1 numbers are new, but their direction was pre-signalled. Last year ran the same way: the Sep 2025 upgrade was +22.5% and the Nov 2025 interims, which said 'in line', moved +0.4%. Every finding is a small proxy and they offset (sum -0.05), so p_up is 51. abs_move is 5.0, set from this name's own interim and full-year days (0.4 to 22.5%, median about 4.6%) and not shrunk for the sign.

findings.finding: H1 FY27 laps a weak comparator: H1 FY26 revenue was £196.1m (+7%) and adjusted PBT fell to £32.0m from £38.2m. FY27 consensus is now about +25% on both lines, so the headline growth rates will be large, but the August upgrade already told the market this.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025 interims, which followed the Sep 2025 upgrade and said 'in line', moved +0.43%. Nov 2024 interims +6.2%, Nov 2023 (a cut) -22.5%
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The 18 Aug RNS and the +22% move put the strength into consensus. What is not public is the H1 split, so only a beat inside the upgraded FY would be new.

findings.finding: Margin risk from delivery capacity: in FY26 contractor costs rose to £18.5m from £4.5m and third-party suppliers to £30.1m from £14.7m to staff large new contracts, and the adjusted margin fell to 16% from 18%. If the new contracts are still ramping in H1, margin quality could disappoint even if revenue beats.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: May 2025 FY results, a margin-led reaction, -7.4%; May 2026 (margin down, revenue strong) +0.7%
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference. The August update said PBT would be 'comfortably ahead' too, and Berenberg models PBT growing in line with revenue (margin flat at about 15.5%), so a further margin slip on contractor mix would not be in that model. Because the company guided PBT up, the finding is kept small.

findings.finding: Workday, the counterparty for about 40% of Kainos revenue (Workday Services and Products), reported on 27 Aug: Q2 FY27 subscription revenue +13.9%, a raised FY subscription guide of $9.94-9.95bn, and 12-month subscription backlog +14.2%. The ecosystem is healthy through Kainos's H1.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a counterparty proxy and has been public for ten weeks, so it is mostly priced. It only confirms the Workday lines will not be a drag.
findings.independence: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/kainos-group--knos/trading-update/9726177 (Kainos: double-digit growth in both Workday divisions)

findings.finding: Accenture's Q4 FY26 (1 Oct) had record big-ticket bookings (141 deals of $100m or more, book-to-bill 1.2), and the stock rose about 20% as fears of AI disruption to IT services eased. That is a better sector backdrop for the multiple Kainos's interims will be read against.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: KNOS went from 1,200p (2 Oct) to 1,341p (26 Oct) after it
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: KNOS rallied in October. It is a peer sentiment proxy only.

findings.finding: Long holders have been sellers into strength: QUBIS (Queen's University) cut from 9.82% to 8.67% on 3 Sep and Baillie Gifford from 5.95% to 4.50% on 5 Oct. The stock slid 7.8% from 1,341p (26 Oct) to 1,237p (6 Nov) into the print.
findings.why_not_priced: Public TR-1s and visible in the tape. The supply overhang may cap a beat, while the drift lowers the bar going in; the two roughly offset.

findings.finding: Kainos's new Pay Transparency product, resold exclusively by Workday, depends on the EU Pay Transparency Directive. 23 of 27 member states missed its 7 June 2026 transposition deadline, which could slow adoption of a Workday Products growth driver.
findings.why_not_priced: This is macro-to-company transmission and the company has not said anything about it. The product is a small slice of Workday Products ARR (£89m of a £431m group), and first employer reports are still due in June 2027, so it is sized very small and net of the rest of the company.

findings.finding: Capital return: the last buyback finished on 15 May 2026 and none has run since (no Transaction in Own Shares RNS after 18 May). Cash was £89.1m at March with no debt. Last year's renewal came on 19 Nov 2025, nine days after the interims, so a new programme or a higher interim dividend could come with these results.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 19 Nov 2025 buyback renewal: no isolated move measured
findings.why_not_priced: The timing is uncertain. Last year's renewal came separately and after the interims, so the window may not see it; it is sized small for that reason.

lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the weak-comparator H1 finding was cut from +0.3 to +0.1 because the August upgrade pre-signalled H1 strength; p_up moved from 52 to 51
'Size the move on what is new; let the reaction history move p_up, not abs_move': abs_move kept at 5.0 despite last year's +0.4% interims, because the H1 numbers and any guidance wording are new
